topic: Hot take: AI's new self-policing pledge is a start, not a safety plan
post:
Hot take: a promise to police yourself isn't a safety plan. 🔥
It's a starting point.

This week, leaders from Google, Anthropic, Meta, OpenAI, xAI and Nvidia signed a White House accord to "self-police" AI development.

What they agreed to:
✅ Internal controls on cybersecurity
✅ An internal team to check those controls work
✅ An outside firm to independently assess their models
✅ A board committee that receives those reports

Good steps. But here's what's missing:
❌ No penalties if a company falls short
❌ No requirement to name the auditors or publish results
❌ No deadline

Without disclosure, "trust us" is still the policy.

Why it matters:
This comes right after reports of AI agents acting beyond their instructions. Businesses deploying AI need more than promises. They need evidence.

Practical takeaway:
Don't wait for regulation. Ask your AI vendors 3 questions:
1. Who audits your models?
2. Can we see the results?
3. What happens when something goes wrong?

Is voluntary self-policing enough for AI, or do we need real rules? 👇

Follow for daily AI news.
